title: Telling Time to the Minute; a.m. and p.m.
seo_title: Grade 2 Telling Time to the Minute Worksheets (TEKS 2.9G)
standard_text: 2.9G read and write time to the nearest one-minute increment using analog and digital clocks and distinguish between a.m. and p.m.
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 time worksheets for Texas TEKS 2.9G: count by 5s around the clock, read clocks to 5 minutes and to the minute, time words and a.m. and p.m. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Count by 5s, then count on by 1s.
key_sub: Short hand: hour. Long hand: minutes. a.m. morning, p.m. afternoon and evening.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes.
  • Count by 5s for each number on the clock, then count on by 1s for the little marks.
  • a.m. is from midnight to noon (morning). p.m. is from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening).

Examples

Example

Short hand just past 3, long hand 2 marks after the 7

7 × 5 = 35, + 2 = 37

Answer: 3:37

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up the handsThe short hand is the hour.
Reading the minute hand as its numberThe long hand on 4 means 20 minutes.
Mixing up a.m. and p.m.Breakfast is a.m.; dinner is p.m.

faq.a: Read and write time to the nearest one-minute increment using analog and digital clocks and distinguish between a.m. and p.m.

items.q: The long hand moves from the 12 to the 3. How many minutes go by?
items.e: Count by 5s for each number: 5, 10, 15. 15 minutes go by.

items.q: The long hand moves from the 12 to the 8. How many minutes go by?
items.e: Count by 5s for each number: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. 40 minutes go by.

items.q: The long hand goes all the way around, from the 12 back to the 12. How much time goes by?
items.e: 12 numbers × 5 minutes = 60 minutes. 60 minutes is 1 hour.

items.q: It is 10 minutes after the hour. Where does the long hand point?
items.e: Count by 5s: 5 is the 1, 10 is the 2. (The 10 on the clock means 50 minutes.)

items.q: It is 40 minutes after the hour. Where does the long hand point?
items.e: Count by 5s until you say 40: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. That is 8 numbers, so the long hand is on the 8.

items.q: How many minutes are in 1 hour?
items.e: The long hand goes all the way around the clock once in one hour: 60 minutes.

items.q: How many minutes are in half an hour?
items.e: Half of 60 minutes is 30 minutes.

items.q: How many minutes are in a quarter hour?
items.e: A quarter is one of 4 equal parts. 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes.

items.q: School starts in the morning. Which time could it be?
items.e: a.m. is from midnight to noon (night and morning). p.m. is from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening). The answer is 8:00 a.m.
a.m. is from midnight to noon (night and morning). p.m. is from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening). The answer is 3:15 p.m.

items.q: You eat dinner in the evening. Which time could it be?
items.e: a.m. is from midnight to noon (night and morning). p.m. is from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening). The answer is 6:30 p.m.

items.q: Which time is after midnight and before noon?
items.e: a.m. is from midnight to noon (night and morning). p.m. is from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening). The answer is 7:20 a.m.

items.q: You go to bed at night. Which time could it be?
items.e: a.m. is from midnight to noon (night and morning). p.m. is from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening). The answer is 9:00 p.m.
10:45 is 15 minutes before 11:00, so it is quarter to 11.
4:30 is 30 minutes after 4:00, so it is half past 4.
10:15 is 15 minutes after 10:00, so it is quarter past 10.

items.q: Valeria eats breakfast before school. What time could it be?
items.e: Breakfast is in the morning, so it is an a.m. time: 7:15 a.m.

items.q: Caleb wakes up for school. What time could it be?
items.e: Waking up for school happens in the morning. Morning times are a.m.: 6:45 a.m.

items.q: School starts. What time could it be?
items.e: School starts in the morning, so it is a.m.: 8:05 a.m. (3:05 a.m. is the middle of the night.)

items.q: Diego plays outside at morning recess. What time could it be?
items.e: Morning recess is during the school day, before noon. That is a.m.: 10:20 a.m.

items.q: Marcus rides the bus home from school. What time could it be?
items.e: School ends in the afternoon. Afternoon times are p.m.: 3:10 p.m.

items.q: Jayden eats a snack after school. What time could it be?
items.e: After school is the afternoon. Afternoon times are p.m.: 3:45 p.m.

items.q: Lucia eats dinner with her family. What time could it be?
items.e: Dinner is in the evening. Evening times are p.m.: 6:00 p.m.

items.q: Elijah goes to bed at night. What time could it be?
items.e: Going to bed happens at night, after noon and before midnight. That is p.m.: 8:30 p.m.

items.q: Ava is fast asleep. It is the middle of the night. What time could it be?
items.e: After midnight a new day starts, and the times are a.m. The middle of the night is a time like 2:00 a.m.

items.q: It is 9:00 p.m. What is Gabriel most likely doing?
items.e: 9:00 p.m. is late in the evening, so Gabriel is most likely sleeping. At 9:00 a.m. he would be at school.

items.q: It is 7:00 a.m. What is Zoe most likely doing?
items.e: 7:00 a.m. is early in the morning, before school, so Zoe is most likely eating breakfast. Dinner and bedtime are p.m.

items.q: It is 4:15. What time will it be in 1 hour?
items.e: In 1 hour the short hand moves to the next number. The minutes stay the same. 4:15 → 5:15. (4:16 is only 1 minute later.)
The clock shows 2:40. In 1 hour the hour goes up by 1 and the minutes stay the same: 3:40.

items.q: It is 2:10. What time will it be in 30 minutes?
items.e: Count on by 5s from the 2: 30 minutes is 6 numbers. The long hand goes from the 2 to the 8. 2:10 → 2:40. (3:10 is 1 hour later, not 30 minutes.)

items.q: It is 9:45. What time will it be in 30 minutes?
items.e: Count on 15 minutes to 10:00, then 15 more minutes: 10:15. The long hand went past the 12, so the hour goes up to 10.

items.q: Nevaeh's soccer practice starts at 4:30 p.m. It lasts 1 hour. What time does it end?
items.e: 1 hour after 4:30 is 5:30. It is still the afternoon, so it is 5:30 p.m.

items.q: Isabella gets to the park at 10:15 a.m. She stays for 1 hour. What time does she leave?
items.e: 1 hour after 10:15 is 11:15. It is still before noon, so it is 11:15 a.m.

items.q: Ethan's piano lesson starts at 2:00 p.m. It lasts half an hour. What time does it end?
items.e: Half an hour is 30 minutes. 2:00 + 30 minutes = 2:30 p.m. (2:15 is only a quarter hour later.)

items.q: Carlos starts his homework at 3:40 p.m. He works for 30 minutes. What time does he finish?
items.e: Count on 20 minutes from 3:40 to 4:00. Then 10 more minutes: 4:10 p.m. The long hand went past the 12, so the hour changed from 3 to 4.

items.q: Mateo's swim class starts at 5:45 p.m. It lasts 30 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Count on 15 minutes from 5:45 to 6:00. Then 15 more minutes: 6:15 p.m. (5:15 p.m. forgets that the hour changed.)
